item.title: Top stocks to watch today: Bharti Airtel, HDFC Bank, LG Electronics, Lupin, Alembic Pharma, KSB and 7 others in focus
item.description: Indian markets are poised to open higher on Thursday after the Sensex and Nifty surged nearly 2% on Wednesday, supported by foreign inflows, softer crude and bank-stock buying. Investors will track corporate updates from companies including HDFC Bank, Bharti Airtel, Lupin and LG Electronics India.

item.title: Situational Awareness Lost 65% in Wild Third Quarter, Report Says
item.description: Situational Awareness told investors it lost 65% after fees in the third quarter, after highly levered bets on artificial intelligence firms nearly led to the hedge fund’s implosion in July, according to the Wall Street Journal.

item.title: Stock market outlook today,26 Nov:Sensex, Nifty prediction-DJIA, S&P, NASDAQ, GIFT Nifty, Kospi, Nikkei, Taiwan cues
item.description: Indian markets are poised to open higher today, supported by positive Asian trading and a premium in Gift Nifty. Sensex and Nifty surged Wednesday on foreign inflows, softer oil prices and bank-stock gains. Analysts see a bullish outlook but advise buying on dips, with key resistance near 26,000.

item.description: Indian stocks rebounded on Wednesday, with the Sensex rising 1.82% and Nifty 1.85%, supported by lower crude prices and foreign investor buying. Nagaraj Shetti recommended Devyani Intl and DOMS Industries for a 2–3-week trade, while noting key Nifty support at 25,400 and resistance near 26,000.

item.title: Would-Be RadioShack Revivers Settle SEC Fraud Suit Allegations
item.description: Three entrepreneurs accused of misleading investors about pandemic-era plans to revive distressed retailers including RadioShack and Pier 1 Imports agreed to pay more than $6.8 million to end a US regulator’s lawsuit claiming they were running a Ponzi-like scam.

item.title: Anthropic’s Stock Sparks Rare Divide Inside One Wall Street Firm
item.description: Two equity analysts at a single Wall Street research firm have taken the unusual step of posting conflicting views on the outlook for the hottest stock in the market: Anthropic PBC’s newly listed shares.

item.title: JPMorgan Sees $450 Billion AI Debt Blitz in 2027 Before Plateau
item.description: Companies will tap public high-grade debt markets for $450 billion next year to finance their artificial intelligence-related capital expenditures, even as a growth plateau looms for the burgeoning industry further down the road, according to analysts at JPMorgan Chase & Co.

item.description: The plunge in the value of Bitcoin is putting pressure on billion-dollar mining companies to liquidate their remaining token reserves, both to cover steep operating costs and to fund an increasingly strained pivot into AI data centers.

item.title: Nasdaq 100 plunges nearly 5%, briefly enters bear-market zone as AI fears and fresh tariffs hit sentiment
item.description: US stocks fell sharply as investors sold AI-related shares over concerns about heavy investment, borrowing costs and future returns. The Nasdaq 100 briefly entered bear-market territory, while hotter-than-expected inflation and proposed US tariffs added to market jitters.

item.title: MCX gold plunges ₹4,420/10g, silver sheds nearly ₹8,800/kg as PCE data fuels December Fed rate hike bets
item.description: Gold and silver extended their sharp declines as hotter-than-target US inflation strengthened expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes and lifted the dollar. MCX gold fell 3.6% to ₹1,17,906 per 10 grams, while silver dropped ₹8,800 to ₹1,36,712 per kg.

item.title: Nifty recovers Monday's losses, moves within reach of record high
item.description: Indian equities have emerged as Asia's best-performing market this month, with the Nifty 50 gaining 12% as foreign investors poured nearly $15 billion into domestic stocks.

item.title: Nvidia stock loses momentum after Huang's return as CEO, down another 9%; why are investors dumping AI stocks again?
item.description: Nvidia shares fell 9% at Wednesday’s open, extending a two-day decline to 14.5% as investors weighed rising AI infrastructure costs, higher borrowing costs, governance uncertainty and potential regulation.&nbsp;

item.title: LG Electronics shares to be in focus as promoter to sell 2% stake to meet public float norms; check details
item.description: LG Electronics Inc. plans to sell up to 2% of LG Electronics India through a block deal at a floor price of ₹1,709.30 per share, raising about ₹2,320.5 crore to meet minimum public shareholding rules. The sale would reduce the promoter’s stake from 85% to 83%.

item.title: Corporate bond fundraising set for record in FY27 despite rising borrowing costs
item.description: As of 23 November, corporate bond issuances through private placements had already touched ₹7.16 trillion in FY27, according to Prime Database. With over four months remaining in the financial year, borrowing may reach or even surpass the previous record of ₹11.03 trillion, achieved in FY25.

item.title: Schaeffler India block deal: Schaeffler AG likely to sell 6% stake at ₹3,400 apiece; deal size ₹3,188 crore: Report
item.description: Schaeffler AG is reportedly planning to sell a 6% stake in Schaeffler India through a block deal worth about ₹3,188 crore, at a 5.6% discount to the previous close. The proposed sale comes as the stock extends its decline, despite strong September-quarter profit and revenue growth.

item.title: BSE, Eternal, Titan, SBI among 18 Nifty 50 stocks that rallied 10–43% in 2026; what's driving gains?
item.description: Indian equities rebounded in November as lower oil prices, stronger earnings and renewed foreign investment improved sentiment. Eighteen Nifty 50 stocks rose 10% to 43% in 2026, led by BSE, while the index climbed 12% in November.

item.title: Gold price prediction: Despite 27% decline from January peak, UBS still retains ₹1.50 lakh/10 gram target for 2027
item.description: UBS has maintained its Attractive rating and forecast that gold will reach $5,000 per ounce by December 2027, despite a sharp recent decline. The bank cites central-bank buying, rising sovereign debt, geopolitical uncertainty and Chinese demand as long-term supports.

item.description: NSE shares rose 5% to a record ₹2,324 after ICICI Securities initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a ₹2,650 target. The brokerage cited market leadership, rising retail participation and new growth areas, and forecast strong revenue and profit growth through FY29.

It cites India’s transmission investment cycle, the company’s specialised HVDC products, expanding capacity and strong order book as growth drivers.

item.title: Rollercoaster ride in stock market today: Nifty pares gains by 270 points, Sensex crashes over 800 from day's high
item.description: Sensex and Nifty rose today, supported by foreign fund inflows and lower oil prices, but surrendered much of their early gains as investors booked profits. Weak Asian markets and overnight US losses weighed on sentiment, leaving traders cautious ahead of key Nifty support and resistance levels.

item.title: FIIs back with a bang! Inflows return to Indian stocks after 2-month sell-off; 14 sectors attracted foreign money | List
item.description: Foreign investors poured $13 billion into Indian equities over 14 November trading sessions, reversing September and October outflows. Lower oil prices, easing geopolitical concerns, attractive valuations and stronger-than-expected earnings supported the rebound.

item.title: MCX rates: Gold crashes 13%, silver plunges 20% in Nov 2026; is worst over? What should precious metals investors do?
item.description: MCX rates: Gold and silver have plunged in November as a stronger dollar, higher US yields and investors unwinding positions pressure prices. Analysts say both metals are deeply oversold, but warn that further declines remain possible.

item.title: Traders pull back from closing auction ahead of Sebi’s revised framework
item.description: Sebi will restore the 30-minute VWAP calculation on derivatives expiry days while retaining CAS on other trading days, leaving traders to operate under two different closing-price mechanisms.
